cl. 1. P. अर्घति, to be worth, be of value, Pañcat.;
 (cf. √ अर्ह्)
, worth, value, price, Mn. Yājñ.
(often ifc. cf. धनार्घ॑, महार्घ, शतार्घ॑, सहस्रार्घ॑)
respectful reception of a guest (by the offering of rice, durva-grass, flowers, or often only of water), ŚBr. xiv, &c. (often confounded with अर्घ्य, q.v.)
a collection of twenty pearls (having the weight of a Dharaṇa), VarBṛS.
a sort of yellow bee, L.
अर्घ—दान n. presentation of a respectful offering.
अर्घ—पात्र n. (for अर्घ्य-पात्र) the small vessel in which water is offered to the guest on his arrival, Kathās.
अर्घ—बलाबल n. rate of price, proper price, the cheapness or dearness of commodities, Mn. ix, 329 (cf. अर्घस्य ह्रासं वृद्धिं व, Yājñ. ii, 249). =

अर्घ—संस्थापन n. fixing the price of commodities, appraising, assize (it is the act of a king or ruler, in concert with the traders, and should be done once a week or once a fortnight), Mn. viii, 402.
‘diminution of price’
अर्घापच˚येन ind. instr. cheaper, Gaut.
worthy of or requiring a respectful offering, a superior.
N. of Śiva, (cf. अर्घीश)
(‘अर्घिन्’ for अर्घ) = अर्घेश्वर, q.v., L.
‘valuable’, see अन्-अर्घ्य, (g. दण्डादि, q.v., ‘अर्घम्-अर्हति’) deserving a respectful reception (as a guest), PārGṛ.; Yājñ. &c.
belonging to or used at the respectful reception of a guest, Gobh.; Yājñ. &c.
(Pāṇ. v, 4, 25) water offered at the respectful reception of a guest, ĀśvGṛ. &c., (probably for आर्घ्य, q.v.) a kind of honey, L.
relating to or coming from the above bee, Suśr.
its honey, L.

अर्घ्य—पात्र n. See अर्घ-प्˚.
अर्घ्य—शील mfn. of deferential character or disposition, R.
the plant Pterospermum Suberifolium, L.
(= पार्घट, q.v.) ashes, L.
